sections.overview: The Tawny-barred Angle is a geometrid moth associated with coniferous woodland in Britain.
sections.identification: Its wingspan is 22–27 mm; the dark form nigrofulvata is reported especially often in northern Britain.
sections.habitat: The British account describes it as fairly common through much of the islands, in landscapes with conifer woodland.
sections.diet: Its caterpillars feed on conifers, especially Scots pine.
sections.behavior: A Finnish species account says it flies at dusk and at night and is attracted to light.
sections.reproduction: In Finland, the pupa overwinters; local flight timing differs from the British pattern.
sections.ecology: Like Macaria signaria, it is a congener whose larvae use conifers, although Scots pine is especially noted for this species.
sections.conservation: UKMoths describes it as fairly common in much of Britain; that regional account does not establish a global population trend.
